title: National Aluminium Company Ltd - 532234 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: NALCO FY26 revenue rose 6.28% to Rs.17,843 crore and PAT 9.22% to Rs.5,816 crore, with FY27 alumina guidance of about 25 lakh tons.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as the best ever year on physical output, sales and financials, with revenue from operations up 6.28% to Rs.17,843 crore, EBITDA up 8.72% to Rs.8,613 crore and PAT up 9.22% to Rs.5,816 crore. Alumina realisation fell from about $580/t (FY25) to about $370/t (FY26), offset by higher volumes and a metal realisation rise to about $2,700/t. Management guided to lower alumina prices of $300-310/t for FY27 and LME averaging around $3,000-3,100/t as Middle East smelter curtailments unwind. The 5th stream refinery (2 lakh t) is scheduled for commissioning from June 2026, with the smelter and captive power plant project (0.5 mtpa) planned for ordering in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of Rs.135 crore in FY25; Q4 profit of Rs.11 crore

segments.name: Alumina
segments.commentary: FY26 sales volume about 23 lakh t vs 20.75 lakh t production in FY25; price effect of about Rs.2,659 crore offset by about Rs.1,714 crore volume benefit, net adverse impact about Rs.784 crore. Domestic sales rose to about 1.37-1.4 lakh t from 40,000 t, exports about 13.09 lakh t.

segments.name: Aluminium (metal)
segments.commentary: FY26 cast metal production about 4.71 lakh t (+2.61%), capacity 4.6 lakh t; FY27 plan 4.73 lakh t. Pricing is linked to LME with export premium fixed via six-monthly export tenders; no hedging. Q1 FY27 realisation guided at about $3,500-3,600/t for the quarter.

segments.name: Chemical (caustic soda / chlor-alkali)
segments.commentary: Chemical segment revenue fell about 12% from Rs.7,600 crore to Rs.6,694 crore as per the analyst's figures; management cited lower alumina-linked pricing. Caustic soda cost rose from about Rs.42,177/t average in FY26 to about Rs.45,000/t expected in Q1-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Coal (Utkal captive)
segments.commentary: Captive production about 4.0 mt in FY26 (+41.84%), target 4.8 mt in FY27 against total requirement of about 7.2 mt. Captive coal cost about Rs.1,500/t vs linkage about Rs.1,800/t and E-auction about Rs.2,100/t.

guidance_outlook: FY27 alumina production and sales planned at about 25 lakh t, around 2 lakh t above FY26; management said 2 lakh t is the minimum and could reach 3-3.5 lakh t depending on commissioning.
FY27 alumina realisation expected at $300-310/t average, with spot at $310-320/t; management cited surplus from Indonesian refineries and Middle East smelter curtailments.
FY27 LME average expected around $3,000-3,100/t once the Middle East supply disruption normalises; spot LME was about $3,550-3,600/t in April 2026.
Management expects FY27 PBT to stay above about Rs.2,000 crore per quarter run-rate if volumes hold and cost does not rise; alumina price decline seen as offset by metal prices.
Employee cost guided lower in FY27 as about 250 superannuations are offset by recruitment; pay revision impact of 10-15% expected from January 2027 (FY28 onwards).

Capex: about Rs.2,000 crore in FY26-27, Rs.4,000-5,000 crore in FY27-28, peaking at Rs.8,000-10,000 crore in FY28-30 for the 0.5 mtpa smelter (about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore) and power plant (about Rs.12,000 crore, to be shared 50:50 with NLC JV).
capex_capacity: 5th stream alumina refinery (2 lakh t): commissioning to start June 2026, taking 3-4 months to reach 50-60% of rated capacity; about one to two months delay possible. Capital work in progress about Rs.6,300 crore, of which about Rs.5,500 crore relates to the 5th stream and is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

Proposed 0.5 mtpa aluminium smelter with 270 MW captive power plant: DPR and technology licensor under way; board approval targeted around Aug-Sep 2026; tendering 6-7 months; groundwork from around April-May 2027; completion targeted December 2030 to early 2031.
Power plant to be a 50:50 JV with Neyveli Lignite Corporation (MoU signed, advanced negotiations), with NLC's Talcher coal mine nearby for coal security.
Additional wire rod mill of about 60,000 t (roughly two years) and MI annealing furnace to lift rolled products from about 2,000 t/month to 2,500 t/month.
Utkarsh JV with Mishra Dhatu Nigam discontinued; the Board cited negative IRR on a Rs.4,500-5,000 crore capex plan.
Captive coal target 4.8 mt in FY27; EC clearance for the enhanced coal output expected in about three to four months.
demand_pricing: Middle East smelter curtailments (Qatalum, EGA, Dubal and one other, cut around 50%) reduced alumina demand; Middle East used to take about 40-50% of alumina exports.
Spot alumina tenders recently at $310-336/t; company is relying only on spot tenders with no long-term contracts at present. Recent long-term contract priced at 11-11.5% of LME versus 15-17% earlier.
Japan and Asian premiums rose sharply; NALCO's export premium is fixed for six months via tenders, with the next export tender expected within a month or two.
Domestic alumina sales target of 2.5-3 lakh t in FY27 (about 1.4 lakh t in FY26).

Input cost trend for Q1 FY27: CP coke about Rs.57,000/t (from Rs.53,000), CT pitch about Rs.57,000/t (from Rs.53,000), aluminium chloride about Rs.1.30 lakh/t (from Rs.1.21 lakh), HFO about Rs.70,000/t (from Rs.46,000). E-auction coal prices reported as flat over the last two months.
Aluminium cost of production about Rs.155,000-160,000/t (FY26 average about Rs.156,000/t); alumina cost about Rs.20,000-22,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 alumina and aluminium volume guidance and the 5th stream ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 alumina target about 25 lakh t (+2 lakh t), metal about 4.73 lakh t vs capacity 4.6 lakh t. 5th stream commissioning starts June 2026 with 3-4 months to stabilise; one-two months delay possible.

qa_highlights.question: How much alumina export volume was there and what share goes to the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 exports about 13.09 lakh t and domestic about 1.37 lakh t. Middle East historically took 40-50% of exports, now sharply reduced; no volume impact yet per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 0.5 mtpa smelter capex be phased and what are the numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about Rs.4,000-5,000 crore in FY28 (in management's FY27-28 wording), rising to Rs.8,000-10,000 crore in FY29-30 peak; total smelter about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore and power plant about Rs.12,000 crore, with JV share reducing NALCO's cost to about Rs.23,000-24,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the employee cost and other expenses jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said employee cost fell 18% to 15% YoY, with about 351 retirements and 358 inductions in FY26 saving about Rs.65 crore. Other expenses included about Rs.40 crore red mud pond provision and Rs.54 crore additional fly ash transport provision, which are non-cash.

qa_highlights.question: What are alumina and aluminium price expectations for FY27 and what is the margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Alumina $300-310/t average; LME about Rs.3,000-3,100/t on average. Management said the metal price gain (about $400/t vs FY26 at $3,000-3,100) would offset alumina decline; metal is about 73% of revenue vs 27% alumina.

qa_highlights.question: What is the coal mix and cost per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Total requirement 7.2 mt; captive 4.8 mt target FY27 (4.0 mt FY26); balance mainly FSA linkage from Coal India, with e-auction only 10-15%. Captive about Rs.1,500/t, linkage about Rs.1,800/t, e-auction about Rs.2,100/t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the wage revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Pay revision from January 2027 expected to raise employee cost 10-15% (possibly 12-13%) in FY28; FY27 impact estimated around Rs.100 crore additional, per management. Per-tonne cost expected to fall with volume growth.

risks_watch: 5th stream alumina refinery (2 lakh t): commissioning from June 2026 with 3-4 months to stabilise; management flagged one to two months possible delay, and FY27 alumina volume upside depends on commissioning pace.
Alumina price pressure: spot at $310-320/t, management guiding $300-310/t average for FY27; no long-term contracts currently, and the long-term contract rate fell to 11-11.5% of LME from 15-17%.
Metal price normalisation: management expects LME to fall from about $3,550-3,600/t (April 2026) to about $3,000-3,100/t average, which is central to the margin offset argument.

Input cost inflation in Q1 FY27: HFO up to about Rs.70,000/t from Rs.46,000, CP coke and CT pitch up to about Rs.57,000/t, caustic soda rising to about Rs.45,000/t; management said cost of production would rise but stay within Rs.160,000/t.

Capex and execution: 0.5 mtpa smelter (about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore) and 270 MW power plant (about Rs.12,000 crore, 50:50 JV with NLC) depend on DPR, board approval around Aug-Sep 2026 and the NLC JV agreement; EC clearance for captive coal expansion expected in three to four months.
Wage revision from January 2027 expected to raise employee cost 10-15% in FY28; export premium is fixed for six months via tenders, and the next export tender is expected within a month or two.
key_quotes: Today is a historic day for NALCO. The Board of Directors have approved the financial statements for the financial year '25-'26, registering the best ever performance in every front.
So, both areas in alumina and metal, we have looked for the growth.
Two lakh is the minimum we are targeting. It can go to maybe 3 lakh or 3.5 lakhs also, depending on the commissioning process.
It is very difficult to predict now.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 physical and financial performance and on the metal price outlook, with management repeatedly calling results the best ever. Noticeably cautious and vague on alumina pricing beyond FY27 and on the timing and size of the 5th stream ramp-up, and on Middle East export volumes, where management said it was very difficult to predict.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27 (alumina ~25 lakh t, metal 4.73 lakh t)
rows.why: Alumina output and sales guided at about 25 lakh t versus about 23 lakh t sold in FY26 (+2 lakh t), and metal production of 4.73 lakh t versus 4.71 lakh t in FY26 against 4.6 lakh t capacity, with domestic alumina sales targeted at 2.5-3 lakh t versus 1.4 lakh t.

rows.why: Smelter (0.5 mtpa, about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore) and 270 MW captive power plant (about Rs.12,000 crore, 50:50 with NLC) have DPR and technology licensor under way, with board approval targeted Aug-Sep 2026 and tendering of 6-7 months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 alumina volume of about 25 lakh t is a minimum and could reach 3-3.5 lakh t of upside depending on commissioning, and Q1 FY27 metal realisation guided at $3,500-3,600/t versus $2,767/t in Q4 FY26.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 alumina realisation guided to $300-310/t versus about $370/t in FY26 and spot at $310-336/t, while Q1 FY27 metal realisation is guided at $3,500-3,600/t and LME is expected to fall to $3,000-3,100/t average; input costs rising (HFO Rs.46,000 to Rs.70,000/t, caustic soda to Rs.45,000/t) and 5th stream delay could hit volumes.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new branded product or molecule launches discussed; the only new items are the wire rod mill (about 60,000 t, planned) and MI annealing furnace lifting rolled products from 2,000 to 2,500 t/month, which are minor.

rows.label: Alumina price reset to $300-310/t in FY27
rows.why: Management guided FY27 average alumina at $300-310/t versus about $370/t in FY26 and $580-595/t in FY25, with no long-term contracts and the long-term rate down to 11-11.5% of LME from 15-17%.

rows.label: Middle East alumina export demand loss
rows.why: Middle East smelters cut output around 50%, and the region historically took 40-50% of exports from FY26 exports of 13.09 lakh t; management said volume impact is very difficult to predict.

rows.label: Employee cost reduction in FY27, wage hike in FY28
rows.when: FY27 lower; January 2027 onward for wage revision
rows.why: About 250 superannuations guided to lower FY27 employee cost, while 10-15% pay revision from January 2027 adds about Rs.100 crore in FY27 per management and more in FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 physical and financial records and the metal price outlook, but cautious and vague on alumina pricing beyond FY27, the 5th stream ramp-up timing, and Middle East export volumes; analysts pressed on these points.
